text:
Lucy: starting a canary traffic shift for model-serving in eu-west-1, moving 10% -> 30%.
Sam: nice. seeing anything odd?
Lucy: yes — during the shift the canary pods failed to scale on the gpu-nodegroup. terraform shows the node count drifted.
Lucy: terraform apply wasn't run on the cluster workspace after the autoscaler config change. plan shows desired_count=6 but actual=4.
Jen: ouch. so the canary hit insufficient alloc and kube scheduler started evicting low-priority pods?
Lucy: exactly. controller logs show Pending due to "Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu".
Sahil: any quick mitigation? we can bump fallback to cpu model until nodegroup fixed but that defeats canary objective.
Lucy: attempted an automated gitops rollback but it didn't trigger — the gitops controller reported a hook timeout (pre-stop probe misconfigured on canary deployment).
deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary rollout started for release/rls-2026.03.16-eu
infra-bot: [infra-bot] Terraform drift detected in workspace cluster-eu-west-1: aws_eks_node_group.gpu: desired_count: 6 -> actual: 4
Sam: can someone run: `kubectl describe node <node>` and `kubectl get pods -n model-serving -o wide`? we need to confirm taints and alloc.
Lucy: pasted output in thread (truncated):
```
Events:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2m (x12 over 5m)  default-scheduler  0/4 nodes are available: 4 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
```
Jen: for immediate recovery we can: 1) scale nodegroup manually to 6 via cloud console 2) patch canary to reduce GPU requests 3) pause traffic shift — what's least blast-y?
Sahil: pause traffic and patch canary to `resources.requests.gpu: "0.1"` if model supports it, then re-run shift after infra fix. low risk.
Lucy: pausing traffic now `console: redwood deployment-api -> traffic-weight canary=10%` :pause_button:
Sam: I'll run `terraform apply -target=aws_eks_node_group.gpu` in the cluster workspace and watch for new nodes.
Sam: running `terraform apply` now — will ping once nodes are Ready.
infra-bot: [infra-bot] Terraform apply queued by Sam (CI job #7881). estimated time ~4m.
Lucy: once nodes are up, we should also patch the canary pre-stop probe to avoid hook timeouts — small PR coming.
Jen: SGTM. add an automated check to CI that validates nodegroup desired == actual before traffic shifts — catch drift earlier.
Sahil: also add a cost-bump guard so we don't auto-scale GPUs beyond budget without a manual override.
Sam: Terraform finished, nodes reporting Ready at 1924008998. re-triggering canary traffic shift to 30%.
deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary traffic adjusted to 30% at 1924009015.
Lucy: rollout looks healthy, pods scheduled, no evictions. marking incident as mitigated, follow-ups: patch probe, add pre-shift infra verification, add cost guard.
Jen: filed follow-up tickets: INFRA-834 (pre-shift infra check), DEPLOY-220 (probe fix), FIN-112 (gpu cost guard).
Lucy: thanks all :thumbsup:
